notes.text: Free electives (4, 4 and 6 ECTS in semesters 2 to 4) are slots; the subjects are not listed on the curriculum page.

courses.title: Architecture and Building Culture
courses.content: Examples are used to convey the connection between cultural-historical backgrounds and concrete architectural solutions as well as basic criteria for assessing the cultural significance of buildings (historical, artistic or other cultural significance). Cultural and technical circumstances and conditions of structural transformation (such as change of use and floor plan, appropriate new use, supporting structure, development, energy requirements and thermal refurbishment, lighting) are dealt with by way of example in order to be able to develop the process of iterative optimization in the area of tension between new use and cultural significance in a living building stock. An analysis of a renovation project with regard to one of the following aspects concludes the course: functional transformation, structural-technical transformation, thermal renovation and energy demand, architectural-cultural transformation, transformation of the built environment. Translated with www.DeepL.com/Translator (free version)
courses.learningOutcome: After completing the course, alumni are able to recognize basic connections of cultural backgrounds and architectural examples. Circumstances and boundary conditions of architectural transformation can be classified and explained.

courses.title: Basics of Urban Planning
courses.content: The core of the lecture is the communication of current European tendencies and principles of urban development. In the course of the lecture, the participants are taught the recognition of urban design quality of urban scales such as street space, square, cityscape, quarter, district and city as a whole. In the context of the in-depth exercise, the theoretically learned principles are analytically fed back.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni recognize urban and open space planning as an organizational basis for the optimal design of living spaces and neighborhoods. They understand the meaning of planning and can read and interpret it. They know the importance of defining and designing public spaces.

courses.title: City in climate change
courses.content: In this course, the basic knowledge of urban climate is taught. With the help of simulation and visualization software, urban environmental influences (e.g. heat island effect, air flows, comfort and coziness, noise, particulate matter) are investigated. City models are used to illustrate the effects described.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni are able to understand the importance of urban ecosystems and the significance for neighborhoods and buildings. They will be able to describe the effect of climatic change and its consequences. They acquire basic knowledge of how to apply measures to improve the urban climate and adapt climate change.

courses.title: Communication Skills
courses.content: The course teaches students about different methods of communication, rhetoric and presentation. Common communication models are examined and communication skills are explained on the basis of personality models. By working on case studies, students are prepared for communication situations in groups and companies, particularly in the context of planning processes, and learn about options for different situations. This also includes the ability to make decisions in the above-mentioned context.
courses.learningOutcome: After completing this module, students will be able to apply various methods to confidently handle situations in their everyday professional lives. They will learn to develop strategies that lead to targeted results.

courses.title: Fundamentals of urban infrastructure systems and energy consumption structures
courses.content: Students gain knowledge of a wide variety of infrastructure systems, for example: Energy infrastructure (energy generation, storage, and distribution), water supply, and wastewater systems, transportation systems, waste treatment and recycling. In addition, essential principles and methods for the operation and maintenance of the infrastructure systems in this area are taught.
courses.learningOutcome: In this module, alumni are taught the basics of urban infrastructure systems. The aim is to give the alumni an overview of the different types of infrastructures in an urban environment.

courses.title: Geoinformation Systems and Urban Data Management
courses.content: Geoinformatics is the study of the nature and function of spatial information (geoinformation) and its acquisition, storage, analysis, visualization, interpretation and dissemination. It forms the scientific basis for geographic information systems (GIS). The spectrum ranges from the modeling of geo-objects in space to their schematization in databases against the background of typical GIS applications. The aim of the course is to work out those aspects of geoinformation that deserve special attention when embedded in the general environment of information technology. The course covers the development and management of geographic information databases, analysis and modeling of geospatial data, visualization of geospatial data and information, and application of GIS-based tools. The use of geographic information systems enables quantitative and qualitative methods for spatially distributed analysis of interacting processes occurring at different scales. These range from global urban change, to climate change, to local land use decisions. The main focus of the course is the collection and linking of spatially relevant data, with the aim of revealing problems and issues in order to develop data-based solutions.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni are able to use the elementary specific application possibilities of geoinformation systems (GIS) for their field of activity and know additional possibilities which are given by the use of GIS systems for example in planning processes. The alumni can use the elementary specific application possibilities of geoinformation systems (GIS) for their field of activity and can link these with spatial questions. In this way, they develop possibilities that are given by the use of GIS systems, for example in planning processes.

courses.title: Intruduction week - Ethic and Sustainability
courses.content: Basic knowledge of professional discourses on ethics and sustainability in the context of health and social affairs, information technologies, engineering, media and design, as well as business and tourism is conveyed with the aim of analyzing, evaluating, arguing and reflecting on relevant contexts and integrating them into one's own future-oriented and responsible options for action.
courses.learningOutcome: Through the basic skills and abilities taught, alumni are able to reflect on projects and content in terms of ethical and sustainable aspects.

courses.title: Open Space Planning
courses.content: Introduction to open space planning in an urban context, historical background, current practice. Basic knowledge as well as methodological approaches on different scale levels (city, neighborhood, object) are taught. This includes planning and design at the neighborhood level and is underpinned by current practical examples. Essential is a differentiated consideration of different approaches and procedures, depending on the goal, the planning level and the problems and size of the area to be addressed. The aim of the course is the knowledge of different open space systems, their different users, accessibility, equipment, design quality, spatial, socio-cultural and ecological effects in urban space.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni recognize urban and open space planning as an organizational basis for the optimal design of living spaces and neighborhoods. They understand the meaning of planning and can read and interpret it. They know the importance of defining and designing public spaces.

courses.title: Revitalization, protection of townscape and architectural monuments
courses.content: Based on the different protection goals of townscape protection and structural monument protection, the design, legal, organizational and technical aspects of townscape and monument protection are dealt with and illustrated with examples. On the basis of a self-selected example project of a redevelopment measure in the local image or monument protection, the concrete legal and organizational framework conditions as well as the design and technical solutions are analyzed and described and possible alternatives are shown.
courses.learningOutcome: Upon completion of the course, alumni will be able to explain and differentiate processes and legal frameworks in the protection of sites and monuments as well as to analyze and fundamentally assess simple questions under guidance.

courses.title: Spatial Planning
courses.content: Participants will learn the basic legal principles of spatial planning and current strategies of Austrian and European cities. The focus is on teaching the Austrian and European legal framework and the associated spatial planning processes such as regional development concept, urban development concept, zoning plans and development plan and building guidelines.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni recognize spatial planning as an organizational basis for the optimal design of living spaces and regions. They understand the significance of zoning plans and development plans and can read and interpret them. They know about the meaning and effects of the plans in the built environment.

courses.title: Urban Ecology
courses.content: The importance of blue and green infrastructure in the urban environment as a basis for planning is explained to the students. For this purpose, the basic terms of the respective areas are explained in order to enable a fundamental understanding. In addition, the perception regarding the quality of human stay in the city (e.g. emissions, climate, etc.) will be sensitized by city walks. In the course of this, the previously theoretically described infrastructure elements are also considered in their actual form.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni know how green and blue infrastructure can be used in planning as necessary measures to improve the urban climate. They have knowledge of various factors influencing the city and can identify problems arising from urban environmental influences and can accordingly call in experts to develop improvement measures.

courses.title: Urban Lab
courses.content: The Urban Lab is the entry project, which pursues an integral planning approach. Based on a common task that combines the focus areas of building in the existing fabric, neighborhood development, and the urban system.
courses.learningOutcome: The project introduces alumni to the topics and problems from the fields of building in existing structures, neighborhood development or urban systems and shows the interconnectedness from each field.

courses.title: Change and Transformation
courses.content: Within the framework of the courses, the students deal with the topic of the implementation of the sustainability goals in the different levels of society. The course is divided into a theoretical part, which includes how processes can be integrated and implemented in the levels of governance (administration and companies) and citizens (individuals and society). Thereby it will be discussed reflexively how structure - process - result of projects are to be classified. On the basis of projects that have already been implemented in practice, methods and approaches will be discussed that can be directly applied to the students' projects. The course is related to the module Participation and Conflict Resolution Strategies.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni receive an overview of how they should address the various topics of transformation (e.g. from the areas of climate and energy change) in terms of content and argumentation in their studies and professional practice, and how already successful courses of action can be implemented in practice.

courses.title: Master seminar I
courses.content: Systematic structure of an exposé and discursive defence of the same in group situations; characteristics of an academic working style; literature phase and thematic breadth (variants); analysis of current publications; handling of academic literature sources, including referencing; quality aspects of academic work.
courses.learningOutcome: A preparatory seminar is held at the end of the second semester to prepare students for their Master's thesis. The course enables graduates to develop independent scientific questions and to proceed systematically and methodically. The seminar includes regular exchanges with other graduates and lecturers to develop the topic of the Master's thesis.

courses.title: Methods of conflict resolution
courses.content: The course provides students with knowledge about different methods for the prevention and resolution of conflicts. By working on different cases, students are prepared for conflict situations in groups and companies, especially in the context of planning processes, and learn about possible solutions for crisis and problem situations.
courses.learningOutcome: After completing this module, alumni will be able to use various methods to develop conflict situations or solution strategies. They will be able to recognize how a clearly structured line of argument can be created to solve conflicts, especially in public participation procedures or in project work. You are able to argue in a solution- and benefit-oriented way and to formulate criticism in a factual and constructive way. You are able to accept criticism and to report it back accordingly.

courses.title: Participation strategies
courses.content: Teaching of guidelines for the practical implementation of participation procedures by means of practical exercises within the framework of several block events, in which real projects are carried out. In the process, a simulation game is carried out, which is aligned with a real project. In this course, students learn how to prepare, implement and evaluate various participation procedures. Questions relevant to practice, such as the redensification of developed inner areas, the removal of car parking spaces and similar issues are dealt with.
courses.learningOutcome: After completing this module, alumni can choose between different participation methods to moderate processes. They learn methods to develop conflict situations or solution strategies. They recognize the structure and characteristics of citizen participation processes and can take an active role in them. The alumni are able to present complex contents in a target group-oriented way and to develop clearly structured lines of argumentation. They can argue in a solution- and benefit-oriented manner and formulate criticism in a factual and constructive manner. They are able to accept criticism and report it back accordingly.

courses.title: Real estate business and project development
courses.content: This course deals with project development in the context of planning processes. This includes: Basics of investment in real estate, market situation, terms, phases, types of property (residential, commercial, logistics, hotel), profitability, location analyses and market data; market participants (developers, planners, investors, construction companies, property owners, tenants, lessees, operators, brokers, key figures); valuation and financing of real estate (asset value, capitalized earnings value, market value); forms of contract, operator models (PPP, etc.)
courses.learningOutcome: The module focuses on project development for initiation, conception and marketing. You take into account relevant economic and legal framework conditions in their implementation.

courses.title: Free elective 1
courses.content: Students are familiar with specific topics in the field of building renovation or urban systems, as well as with topics in related fields, and can successfully apply this knowledge to specific issues in their studies and final thesis.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are familiar with specific topics in the field of building renovation or urban systems, as well as with topics in related fields, and can successfully apply this knowledge to specific issues in their studies and final thesis.

courses.title: Conversion, extension and further construction of existing buildings
courses.content: The LV analyses correlations between building typologies and situations. The consideration of interdependencies makes it possible to derive recommendations for action and fields of action at various planning levels. Functions, building typologies and open space components are examined on the basis of current developments relevant to building regulations. Based on this, conversion and expansion scenarios are developed, which are evaluated technically and functionally and continued as a basis for design.
courses.learningOutcome: After completing the course, graduates will be able to recognise and explain connections between strategic, functional and technical aspects of building typologies and building situations, as well as differentiate between changes in structural transformation processes and their effects. In addition, they will be able to reflect on transformation processes and evaluate them in terms of planning under guidance.

courses.title: Neighborhood development
courses.content: In this course, students learn how to develop project concepts and independently apply general methods to an example from the field of integrated neighbourhood concepts in interdisciplinary teams. Based on an analysis of the current situation, a potential analysis is carried out and an action plan is derived.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are taught the necessary skills to identify, analyse and assess neighbourhoods and evaluate their interactions with the existing context. To this end, they can assess the quality of the existing building structure and identify potential for improvement. They are able to develop qualitative renovation concepts for neighbourhoods and energy supply systems and plan action and implementation strategies.

courses.title: Specialisation Project -Existing Building Structures 2
courses.content: The project in the field of building renovation bridges the gap between theory and practical implementation and introduces students to the diverse range of tasks involved in planning and construction projects.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates can apply the theoretical skills they have acquired in a practical project. This involves using technical skills as well as economic, methodological and social skills.

courses.title: Energy grids & decentralized energy supply
courses.content: This module teaches in-depth competencies in the areas of energy infrastructure and urban energy planning. Depending on the selected courses, the students are able to plan and model electrical transmission and distribution networks as well as thermal local and district heating networks in interaction with various energy supply systems and consumer structures. They know about the possible applications of different electrical and thermal supply and storage technologies and can take these into account in the respective models. Furthermore, the integration of district and local heating networks into the overall urban concept is demonstrated under ecological and economic aspects. The use of renewable energy sources in combination as well as possible line losses are analyzed and included in the holistic view. In addition, district and local heating and cooling networks are modeled and balanced, taking into account the integration of renewable technologies. The understanding for the analysis of such load profiles is trained and applied. Decentralized micro-grids as well as low-temperature district heating networks with cascading heat utilization are also modeled.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni are able to estimate the limits of use of renewable energy sources in urban areas and can develop application-oriented measures to improve their use. They know the essential components of energy planning and can evaluate the different energy sectors (heat, electricity and gas).

courses.title: Energy process engineering
courses.content: This module provides in-depth knowledge in the areas of thermodynamic, advanced and alternative energy conversion processes, environmental protection in thermal energy systems, technical electrochemistry and storage technologies. Furthermore, the integration of district and local heating networks into the overall urban concept is demonstrated from an ecological and economic perspective. The use of renewable energy sources in combination and possible transmission losses are analysed and included in the holistic assessment. In addition, district and local heating and cooling networks are modelled and balanced, taking into account the integration of renewable technologies. Students learn to understand and apply the analysis of such load profiles. Decentralised microgrids and low-temperature district heating networks with cascading heat utilisation are also modelled.
courses.learningOutcome: Absolvent*innen können Verfahren der Abwärmenutzung auswählen, Wissen zu Mehrstoffsystemen in Kälte’, Wärme’ und Kraftmaschinen anwenden, Brennstoffzellen erklären und unterscheiden sowie Konzepte der Meerwasserentsalzung beurteilen und deren Energiebedarf berechnen. Zudem beherrschen sie Verfahren der Abgasreinigung inklusive Entstaubung, Entschwefelung, Entstickung und der Abscheidung spezieller Schadstoffe sowie Methoden der Abgasanalyse.

courses.title: Specialisation Project -Urban Systems 1
courses.content: Students are able to apply the competences acquired in theory within a practical project. In doing so, competences in the technical and engineering field are applied just as much as economic, methodological, and social competences.
courses.learningOutcome: The project in the field of urban infrastructure systems bridges the gap between theoretical content and practical implementation. The Graduates are introduced to interdisciplinary task allocation within the context of specific planning and energy concept projects.

courses.title: Artifical intelligence in city and space
courses.content: The course teaches the basics of AI and its significance for spatial development. It provides an overview of current tools and applications and includes practical sessions with generative AI tools such as Midjourney, Infrared.city and ChatGPT. Possible applications are tested using real-life case studies. Ethical issues, governance and strategies for integrating AI into organisations are also discussed.
courses.learningOutcome: Through the use of artificial intelligence (AI), graduates understand how we plan, design and develop cities and spaces.

courses.title: Master seminar II
courses.content: The accompanying seminar for the Master's thesis aims to establish regular exchange between students and lecturers and, within this framework, to discuss the research topic examined in the Master's thesis. At the same time, milestones are defined through scheduled interim presentations to ensure continuous progress.
courses.learningOutcome: In parallel with the master's thesis, the module supports students in their academic work in a project format. They learn to analyse problems, formulate goals and argue their points in a well-founded manner. Regular exchanges with lecturers and fellow students strengthen their critical thinking, argumentation and discussion skills and provide structured support for the work process.

courses.title: Raw materials and recycling
courses.content: Students are taught the importance of mineral and renewable raw materials and their recycling for planning and development within a curricular economy. Special attention is given to classes of raw materials that are important for sustainability transformations, such as raw materials for the 'Energy Transition' or construction raw materials. Methodological and planning approaches such as Life Cycle Assessments, Urban Mining Indicators or Design for Recycling show the students practical possibilities for a careful use of primary and secondary resources.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni understand the difference and challenges of managing selected raw material groups renewable and mineral raw materials, primary and secondary materials. They understand the principles of different LCAs and design for recycling and can apply them exemplarily.

courses.title: Free elective
courses.content: Students are familiar with specific topics in the field of building renovation or urban systems, as well as with topics in related fields, and can successfully apply this knowledge to specific issues in their studies and final thesis.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are familiar with specific topics in the field of building renovation or urban systems, as well as with topics in related fields, and can successfully apply this knowledge to specific issues in their studies and final thesis.

courses.title: Exploring the existing building stock
courses.content: The course provides in-depth knowledge of how to deal with existing buildings under current transformation requirements. The focus is on conversion and energy-efficient and structural renovation. An existing design is further developed in technical, architectural and strategic terms. In coordination with "Energy in Existing Buildings", details, façades and an energy concept are created that take into account the potential of renewable energy and waste heat and are evaluated in terms of CO’ and feasibility.
courses.learningOutcome: Upon completion of the course, graduates will be able to develop well-considered solutions for building renovation in terms of sustainability and architectural quality. Upon completion of the course, students will be able to develop comprehensive building energy concepts for renovation and revitalisation under supervision, carry out an energy assessment and evaluate the feasibility of the concepts.

courses.title: Neighborhood redevelopment
courses.content: Students acquire basic knowledge for assessing and renovating building structures in neighbourhood redevelopment projects. They learn about urban space types, neighbourhood typologies and energy standards that influence consumption patterns and redevelopment concepts. Various approaches such as renovation, replacement construction or redensification are presented and their advantages and disadvantages for different neighbourhoods are explained.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates are taught the necessary skills to identify, analyse and assess neighbourhoods and evaluate their interactions with the existing spatial context. To this end, they can assess the quality of the existing building structure and identify potential for improvement. They are able to develop qualitative redevelopment concepts for neighbourhoods and plan action and implementation strategies.

courses.title: Specialisation Project -Existing Building Structures 2
courses.content: The project in the field of building renovation bridges the gap between theory and practical implementation and introduces students to the diverse range of tasks involved in planning and construction projects.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates can apply the theoretical skills they have acquired in a practical project. This involves using their technical skills as well as their economic, methodological and social skills.

courses.title: Energy technologies
courses.content: The course covers electrical, thermal and chemical storage technologies as well as the use of renewable energies. Students learn how to calculate the energy balance of storage systems and apply them in decentralised energy concepts. Centralised, decentralised and seasonal storage systems are analysed and calculated. Load profiles are used to optimally adapt storage systems to energy producers and consumers.
courses.learningOutcome: In this module, students acquire in-depth skills in the areas of generating, supplying and storing energy from renewable resources. They are able to evaluate the possible uses of a wide variety of energy resources, as well as their economic viability and efficiency.

courses.title: Municipal technology
courses.content: The course provides detailed knowledge of municipal systems such as drinking water supply, wastewater treatment, transport, waste and recycling. Technological aspects are explained and material and energy flows are analysed in relation to population density. This allows the size of facilities and space requirements for municipal systems to be determined.
courses.learningOutcome: Graduates have knowledge of the possible applications of municipal systems and are able to estimate the scale of these systems in urban areas and develop application-oriented measures for their improved use. They are familiar with the essential components of municipal facilities and can independently develop energy utilisation plans.

courses.title: Specialisation Project -Urban Systems 2
courses.content: Students are able to apply the competences acquired in theory within a practical project. In doing so, competences in the technical and engineering field are applied just as much as economic, methodological, and social competences.
courses.learningOutcome: The project in the field of urban infrastructure systems bridges the gap between theoretical content and practical implementation. The Graduates are introduced to interdisciplinary task allocation within the context of specific planning and energy concept projects.

courses.title: Commission final examination
courses.content: The final examination is held before an examination board and covers the Master’s thesis and subject-related topics.
courses.learningOutcome: The final examination is held before an examination board and covers the Master’s thesis and subject-related topics.

courses.title: International Excursion
courses.content: The aim of the study excursion is to deepen the students' knowledge in the field of building in the existing fabric, neighborhood development or urban systems and to supplement it with application-specific aspects. The excursion to a specific field provides exemplary insights into the concrete design of new and innovative conditions and environments. Students learn to understand and reflect on innovative approaches in the field of building in the existing fabric, neighborhood development or urban systems.
courses.learningOutcome: Through the intensive study of examples of existing buildings, neighborhood development or urban systems, the alumni deepen their knowledge and skills from the previously held relevant modules. Due to the international character of the excursion, the language skills of the alumni are additionally trained.

courses.title: Master seminar III
courses.content: The purpose of the master's thesis colloquium is to establish regular exchange between students and teachers and, within this framework, to discuss the research topic examined in the master's thesis. At the same time, milestones are defined through scheduled interim presentations to ensure continuous progress.
courses.learningOutcome: Parallel to the master's thesis, the module Seminars on the Master's Thesis is held, which supports students in the project format while they are working on their master's thesis. The module enables students to produce independent scientific work and to proceed systematically.

courses.title: Master thesis
courses.content: Development and independent processing of questions and content-related analysis of a subject-relevant topic (core subject areas are the specializations from the areas of building in existing structures, neighborhood development and urban systems) with special consideration of the innovation potential of the targeted solutions, taking into account a scientifically structured and argued at the current state of the literature.
courses.learningOutcome: The master's thesis demonstrates the student's ability to work on a problem from the field of building in the existing fabric, neighborhood development and urban systems using scientific methods. They are able to develop, present and document projects independently and to present and critically evaluate the results in an appropriate manner. They are able to argue and justify their approach scientifically.

courses.title: Free elective
courses.content: The students are familiar with specific topics in the field of building in the existing fabric, neighborhood development or urban systems, but also with specialized topics in related fields and can successfully apply this knowledge to specific questions in the course of study and the final thesis.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni are familiar with specific topics in the field of building in the existing fabric, neighborhood development or urban systems, but also with specialized topics in related fields and can successfully apply this knowledge to specific questions in the course of study and the final thesis.
